Then apply the quadratic formula: x = [-b ± √(b² - 4ac)] / (2a). Calculate the discriminant (b² - 4ac) to determine the nature of the roots—real or complex. Finally, simplify the solutions.

Stationary points occur where the derivative of f(x), f'(x), equals zero. First, compute the first derivative of the function. Then set f'(x) = 0 and solve for x. These x-values are potential stationary points. To confirm whether they’re maxima or minima, check the second derivative (f''(x)): if positive, it’s a minimum; if negative, a maximum.
